[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Robert Glasgow and Isabel Porteous are named as the parents of Mary Glasgow, born 31 July and christened 13 August 1767 at Crawford, and George Glasgow, born 14 May and christened 15 May 1769 in the same parish. The exact parental names, parish and close dates support one household.<ref>[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/60143/records/6989039 Ancestry, Scotland, Select Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950: Mary Glasgow, Crawford, 1767]. Held index transcript; original register uninspected.</ref><ref>[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/60143/records/9156907 Ancestry, Scotland, Select Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950: George Glasgow, Crawford, 1769]. Held index transcript; original register uninspected.</ref>
== Research Notes ==
The source-defined 1769 George now has this Robert selected as father at 98% subjective confidence. His later adult identity remains unknown. William Glasgow-2715 and James Glasgow-3130 remain separate tentative child hypotheses with their existing assessments; this review does not establish their parentage.
A different Robert Glasgow and Isabella Reid had children at New Monkland in 1855, Bathgate in 1857 and Shotts in 1863. Their records were formerly conflated here on the given name Isabel/Isabella. Different maternal surnames and the 96-year span distinguish the households. The later family is maintained separately; no earlier parent or vital field is changed.
Robert's birth, death, marriage date and occupation are unknown. His possible parentage is discussed below.
=== Possible Covington childhood ===
The Robert Glasgow baptised on 12 December 1742 at Covington and Thankerton, son of [[Glasgow-1070|George Glasgow]] and [[Williamson-12853|Agnes Williamson]], is a plausible childhood identity for this Crawford father. He is represented separately by [[Glasgow-1122|Robert Glasgow]]. The age, neighbouring parish setting and later son George support the comparison. The proposed father link is assessed at 55%, possible, including uncertainty over both the adult Robert and the Covington George identities. The two Robert accounts may describe one man; they are not evidence for two brothers. No merger or maternal attachment is proposed.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTLF-SQ7 FamilySearch, Scotland Births and Baptisms, Robert Glasgow, 12 December 1742, Covington and Thankerton]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685660805 Findmypast R_685660805]. Two derivative presentations of the same event; original uninspected.</ref>
